novel_features.name: Route approval that keeps other routes
novel_features.description: Approve a subnet route or exit node on one device without dropping the routes it already has.
novel_features.rationale: The API replaces the whole enabled set on every write, so this reads current routes, merges, re-checks, and verifies instead of sending a blind replacement.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this instead of the raw routes endpoint whenever an agent is asked to enable an exit node or subnet route.

novel_features.name: Route unapproval that keeps other routes
novel_features.description: Remove approval for one route or the exit-node pair while leaving every other approved route in place.
novel_features.rationale: Sends the current enabled set minus the requested routes, read fresh from the device, because the API has no remove-one-route call.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it to turn off an exit node without breaking the subnet routes on the same machine.

novel_features.name: Safe policy entry insert
novel_features.description: Append one nodeAttrs, grants, acls, or ssh entry to the policy file with comments preserved, a local backup, validation, a diff, and a concurrency check.
novel_features.rationale: Combines the HuJSON read, ETag, comment-preserving patch, validate call, and If-Match write that no single endpoint provides.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it whenever an agent needs to add Taildrive, Funnel, or access grants without rewriting the whole policy file.

novel_features.name: Policy rollback
novel_features.description: Roll the policy file back to a local backup after validating it and showing the diff.
novel_features.rationale: Backups live on disk next to the CLI; the restore re-validates and writes with the live ETag so a concurrent change is never overwritten.
novel_features.why_it_matters: This is the undo for every policy write the CLI makes.

novel_features.name: Tailnet route board
novel_features.description: See approved, pending, and stale routes and exit-node state for every device in one table.
novel_features.rationale: Computes advertised-minus-enabled and enabled-minus-advertised across all devices, which the API only exposes one device at a time.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Run it before approving anything to see what is actually waiting.
novel_features.group: Tailnet state an agent can reason about

novel_features.name: Fleet key-expiry report
novel_features.description: List every device by days until its key expires and flag the ones inside a window.
novel_features.rationale: Covers every device in the tailnet from the admin API, not only peers visible from the current machine, and --fail-on-flagged turns it into a cron or CI gate.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it as a weekly check or a CI gate so nobody gets logged out by surprise.
novel_features.group: Tailnet state an agent can reason about

novel_features.name: Machine share audit
novel_features.description: List every machine-share invite across the tailnet with who accepted it and which invites are still redeemable.
novel_features.rationale: The API lists invites per device only; this fans out across all devices and joins the results.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Answer who has access to a shared machine in one call.
novel_features.group: Tailnet state an agent can reason about

novel_features.name: Machine share revoke
novel_features.description: Revoke machine-share invites by ID or by device and acceptor, with a plan before any delete.
novel_features.rationale: Resolves filters to invite IDs from the cross-device share audit, then deletes only those.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it to revoke a contractor's share invites without hunting IDs device by device, then confirm in the admin console that an accepted share is gone.
novel_features.group: Tailnet state an agent can reason about

novel_features.name: Reachability preview
novel_features.description: Show which policy rules let a user reach a device and port, against the live policy or a candidate file.
novel_features.rationale: Resolves the device to its IP, supplies the policy body the preview endpoint needs, and intersects user and ip:port matches.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Check access before and after a policy change without guessing at rule evaluation.

novel_features.name: Device dossier
novel_features.description: Get one device's identity, routes, key expiry, shares, and recent changes in a single record.
novel_features.rationale: Joins the local tailscale status ID with the API device, its invites, and the audit log so an agent has full context before acting.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Make this the first call in any task about a specific machine.

narrative.headline: Tailscale admin from the terminal, with safe route and policy edits an agent can plan before it writes.
narrative.value_prop: Nearly every Tailscale admin API endpoint (tailnet deletion is deliberately left out), plus commands that make the two dangerous whole-object writes safe: routes approve keeps the routes a device already has, and policy add-entry keeps comments, backs up, validates, diffs, and writes with an ETag check. Those safe-write commands (routes approve and unapprove, shares revoke, policy add-entry and restore) write only with --yes and are plan-only as MCP tools; in --agent mode every other mutation is a dry run unless --yes. devices expiry, routes overview, and shares audit answer fleet questions the admin console shows one machine at a time, and access check and devices inspect give an agent one target's full picture before it acts.
narrative.auth_narrative: Create an API access token on the admin console Keys page (https://login.tailscale.com/admin/settings/keys) and export TAILSCALE_API_KEY, or set TAILSCALE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID and TAILSCALE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET to use a scoped OAuth client; the CLI exchanges the client for a short-lived token. The tailnet defaults to '-', meaning the token's own tailnet. Set TAILSCALE_TAILNET only to target a different one.

quickstart.comment: Check config, auth, and API reachability (read-only)
See which device keys expire in the next two weeks
Find routes and exit nodes waiting for approval
Plan an exit-node approval that keeps the device's other routes
List share invites anyone could still redeem

troubleshoots.symptom: HTTP 403 on routes approve or policy add-entry
troubleshoots.fix: The token or OAuth client lacks write scope; use an admin token or add devices:routes / policy_file scopes to the OAuth client

troubleshoots.symptom: policy write fails with 412 precondition failed
troubleshoots.fix: Someone changed the policy since it was read; rerun tailscale-pp-cli policy add-entry to diff against the new version

troubleshoots.symptom: routes approve refuses a CIDR as not advertised
troubleshoots.fix: Advertise it on the device first with tailscale set --advertise-routes, then rerun

troubleshoots.symptom: devices inspect self cannot find this machine
troubleshoots.fix: Install the tailscale command or pass the device hostname or nodeId instead of self

troubleshoots.symptom: doctor says auth is not configured but commands work
troubleshoots.fix: Expected with only TAILSCALE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID/SECRET set; the token is minted per command. Run tailscale-pp-cli routes overview to confirm

troubleshoots.symptom: sync prints sync_warning or sync_error for acl or user-invites
troubleshoots.fix: Non-critical: the policy file is a single document and user-invites returns null when empty; sync still exits 0 and stores devices and users

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI when an agent or operator needs to administer a tailnet: approve routes and exit nodes, edit the policy file, audit or revoke machine shares, check key expiry, or ask which rules allow a connection. It is the right choice when a change must not clobber existing routes or policy content. The device selector self means this machine and needs the local tailscale command; otherwise pass a hostname, MagicDNS name, Tailscale IP, or nodeId.
anti_triggers: Connecting this machine to a tailnet or changing its local settings; use the local tailscale command (tailscale up, tailscale set)
Sending files with Taildrop or serving a local port; use tailscale file and tailscale serve
Managing Headscale or other self-hosted control servers
Deleting a tailnet; that endpoint is deliberately left out, so use the admin console or the API directly
Live free-text search; search only reads data stored locally by sync

recipes.explanation: Prints the before and after enabled routes; rerun with --yes to apply.

recipes.title: Give members Taildrive access
recipes.explanation: Shows the diff and validation result; rerun with --yes to write with the ETag check.

recipes.title: Expiry report for agents
recipes.explanation: Narrows the report to the three fields an agent needs.

recipes.title: Who can reach the NAS over SMB
recipes.explanation: Lists the policy rules that grant access to that device and port.

recipes.title: Roll back the last policy change
recipes.explanation: Shows the diff and validation for restoring the newest local backup; add --yes to restore it, or use --list to pick an older one.
